newsitem.title: CANADA: Fonorola, Ledcor in fibre-optic deal.
newsitem.headline: Fonorola, Ledcor in fibre-optic deal.

text.p: Fonorola Inc said on Thursday it agreed with Ledcor Industries Ltd to begin constructing fibre-optic facility connecting major Canadian cities, with a commitment for the provision of right-of-way from the Canadian National Railway Co.

Fonorola said construction of the facility, connecting Vancouver, Calgary, Edmonton, Winnipeg and Toronto, will begin this autumn in Edmonton and the link between Toronto and Vancouver should be completed by the third quarter of 1998.
It said orders for the optical fibre, which will consist of at least 48 strands, were to be placed by Ledcor near the end of October 1996.

In an associated agreement, CN committed to provide the necessary right-of-way for installation of the connecting link between Edmonton and Toronto, Fonorola said. It said CN supported Ledcor in its efforts to complete the venture, which provides CN with benefits in terms of modernizing its communication and signaling system across the prairies and northern Ontario.

Capital costs on CN's rights-of-way were estimated to be C$120 million, Fonorola said. It said Ledcor was underwriting up to 50 percent of the program cost and would offer fibre-optic strands for sale to third parties who were expected to buy up to three-quarters of the capacity.
